title: Bet Record
description: A bounded venture experiment (`bets/<bet-id>/bet.json` in the portfolio repo, written by scripts/bet.py — see docs/business-factory.md, chief-wiggum#235). A bet is under ~$1k to prove and ~3 months to a kill decision. The embedded `envelope` is a GOALPOST artifact: content-hashed into the portfolio journal at create; `bet.py rebaseline` is the only sanctioned mutation path (Adner & Levinthal 2004 — abandonment conditions must not be retroactively redefined). `state` is maintained by `bet.py transition` only; stage labels are derived from evidence, never self-declared unlocks.

id.description: Stable bet id — the `bets/<id>/` directory name.

thesis.description: The falsifiable thesis this bet exists to test. A pivot closes this bet (criteria evaluated against THIS thesis) and opens a successor with a fresh one.

created.description: ISO timestamp the bet was created.

state.description: proposed → probing → validating → building → scaling; kill_pending reachable from anywhere; terminals killed|parked|lifestyle|sold|wound_down. `killed` is blocked until retrospective.md exists non-trivially and a harvest check ran. `wound_down` (chief-wiggum#274) is a distinct terminal for a PLANNED graceful hold-then-shutdown (or handing the product to a loyal customer) — the normal ending for a small vertical vendor, not a kill, and it carries no retrospective/harvest requirement of its own. `lifestyle` is the LIVE terminal: a revenue-producing, support-consuming product that earns zero in-flight slots forever — its measured ongoing_load feeds the portfolio's attention-capacity accounting (see `bet.py`'s LIVE_STATES).

acquisition.description: The acquisition plan the bet-selection lint reads (chief-wiggum#235 amendment): while means.json says sales/marketing novice and no channel has reached `focused`, a plan with neither an ecosystem channel nor an owned audience is flagged.

ecosystem_channel.description: A built-in-distribution ecosystem channel (marketplace, app store, plugin directory, ...) this bet ships into, or null.

owned_audience.description: An owned audience (list, following, community) the plan draws on, or null.

means_refs.description: References into portfolio means.json entries (skills/assets/network/owned_audience ids or names) this bet draws on — effectuation bird-in-hand: a proposal must reference the means it uses.

harvest_inputs.description: Inputs to the harvest check run before a `killed` transition: est sale value = 3.9 × TTM seller-discretionary profit (Acquire.com micro-SaaS median) vs wind-down cost. Absent inputs → the check reports `skipped`, never blocks silently, never crashes.

wind_down_cost_usd.description: Cost of winding the bet down (time, refunds, contract exits), USD.

unlocked_milestones.description: Milestone ids whose tranches have been unlocked (journaled human acts via `bet.py transition --unlock-milestone`). Invariant: cumulative spend ≤ cumulative unlocked tranches.

rep_cadence_per_week.description: Per-bet rep-cadence override (chief-wiggum#241 leg 3): Mom-Test conversations required per trailing week while probing|validating, counted from the ledger's rep entries. Set at create (`bet.py create --cadence`, journaled); absent → default 3. Missed cadence is a report-only finding feeding the kill review as distribution-not-attempted evidence.

target_cac_usd.description: Target CAC the channel engine (scripts/channel.py, #241) joins measured channel-CAC against for focused channels. Absent → the join reports skipped, never a finding.

headcount.description: Paid heads on this bet (excluding the founder). The channel engine's zero-headcount filter flags sales-led channels (sales, business-development) while this is 0. Absent → falls back to means.json headcount, then 0.

target_load_hours_per_week.description: Per-bet override of the addition-rule target load (chief-wiggum#274, §9.6.3): the most recently added LIVE (lifestyle) product must run below this for two consecutive trailing weekly periods before another bet may start. Absent → defaults to ATTENTION_LOAD_THRESHOLD_HOURS (2h/wk).

mrr_usd.description: Current monthly recurring revenue, USD — operator-entered (not derivable in-repo), unlike ongoing_load which is always measured. Feeds the attention kill criterion (chief-wiggum#274, §9.6.3): a live product costing more than ATTENTION_LOAD_THRESHOLD_HOURS/wk while earning less than ATTENTION_REVENUE_THRESHOLD_USD MRR is a kill-or-redesign candidate. Absent → the check is silent for this bet, never guessed.

signal_tier.description: How contestable this bet's grounding signal is (chief-wiggum#254): A = private signal (inbound requests, personal-network problems, direct operator observation, paid discovery conversations — not in any public corpus). B = semi-public (paid datasets, marketplace analytics behind logins, communities requiring standing). C = public (feature-request boards, review streams, forums) — contested by construction; assume a competitor's agent is reading the same page today. A Tier-C bet without a current `competitor_sweep` is a report-only finding (`bet.py create`/`kill-brief`); absent → the check reports `skipped`, never a crash.

competitor_sweep.description: Create-time competitor sweep (chief-wiggum#254) — run BEFORE a name is picked, not after: the sequencing that missed a real direct-twin collision on the first bet. Stale (>30 days) or absent on a Tier-C bet is a report-only finding, surfaced in `bet.py create` and `kill-brief`.

date.description: ISO date the sweep was run.

sources.description: Where the sweep looked (search engines, marketplace listings, review sites, ...).

competitors.description: Direct competitors found, each with a name and (if known) a URL.

unresolved.description: Anything the sweep could not verify — stated explicitly rather than silently assumed clear.

regulated_calculation_screen.description: Standing screen 15 answers (chief-wiggum#260, docs/business-factory.md §9.5) for a bet whose product computes a number a regulator can audit (wages, tax, super, benefits, clinical dosing, safety thresholds). A bet failing any sub-question is not automatically refused — the mandate is only that the screen is ANSWERED at create time; absent while the thesis names a regulated-calculation domain is a report-only finding (`bet.py create`).

who_bears_error.description: Who bears the error, and does the vendor have (or risk having) system-level knowledge of a defect (FWO v Blue Impression/Ezy Accounting, [2018] FCAFC 134).

correctness_winnable.description: Do incumbents/the regulator's own calculator disclaim accuracy? If so, correctness is not a differentiator.

insurable.description: Is the correctness differentiator actually insurable, or excluded as contractually-assumed liability?

paid_configuration.description: Will the operator do paid configuration work (the Ezy fact pattern) — priced as risk, not revenue.

interpretation_surface.description: Is the rule set bounded and licensable, or unbounded and hand-built?

predecessor.description: Bet id this bet succeeded via a pivot, or null.

successor.description: Bet id opened when this bet was closed by a pivot, or null. Pivot is a transition, not an edit.

low_cap_screens.description: Operator-entered facts for the six low-cap distribution-divergence screens (chief-wiggum#275, docs/business-factory.md §9.6.5 screens 8-13 — candidate additions to the §9.5 standing screens). ALL report-only (docs/gate-rollout.md): findings are printed, never gate, until validated against a real candidate set. Every sub-field absent means that screen is UNRESOLVED (cannot run — a screen that cannot run must say so, never silently pass), not a pass.

enumerable_buyers_count.description: Screen 8: named prospects producible from public sources in an afternoon. Pass window is 500-5,000 inclusive; below 500 is 'no list, no distribution, no business', above 5,000 is the dead zone too big for personal outbound and too small for paid.

support_hazard.description: Screen 9: support-obligation hazard. Reject real-time/critical-path/regulatory-deadline functionality — a solo operator cannot carry an on-call obligation. Reaches the same conclusion as #260's regulated-calculation-liability rabbitry kill from the attention direction rather than liability — the convergence is corroboration, not two overlapping checks.

structural_retention.description: Screen 10: structural retention. Passes if the product stores records the buyer must retain >=5 years, OR runs a weekly-recurring workflow. Satisfaction is not retention.

channels.description: Screen 11: channel existence. Passes if >=1 entry meets its type's bar: association_newsletter cost_usd < 500, trade_show attendees < 5000, member_group members > 2000, or app_marketplace (existence alone is the bar — a browsed marketplace).

dark_matter_demand.description: Screen 12: dark-matter demand. Passes if 10-300 searches/mo across a 10-20 keyword cluster with nonzero CPC, OR >=3 findable 'what software do you use for X' threads. Supersedes the cruder 'reject if search volume is high' heuristic: volume alone is ambiguous, volume-with-commercial-intent is the signal.

opportunity_cost.description: Screen 13: opportunity-cost benchmark. The bet is judged against the operator's contracting rate for the same hours (means.json contracting_rate_usd_per_hour) — never against zero, never against venture outcomes. This is the counterfactual the startup corpus never forces; the ledger had no field for it before #275.

envelope.description: Affordable-loss envelope (Dew et al. 2009 field list), human-set, script-enforced, raisable only via `bet.py rebaseline` (a journaled act with a required --reason).

liability_exposure.description: The affordable-loss envelope's liability/exposure dimension (chief-wiggum#277) — Dew et al.'s 2009 field list omits it, so an uncapped contractual indemnity records identically to no exposure at all. Enumerated, never free text. `bet.py create`/`rebaseline` flag this field's total ABSENCE as a soundness finding; a STATED value — including uncapped_entity/uncapped_personal — is NEVER itself a finding, at create or anywhere else: the operator's risk appetite is a deliberate, sized, counted choice (docs/business-factory.md §9.4 addendum: terms as an undercutting mechanism), not a defect. See also the portfolio-level uncapped-liability concurrency count (`bet.py portfolio`) — one such bet is a considered risk, several concurrently is a portfolio-survival question.

responds.description: Insurability is a separate fact from insurance (#277 decision 2): holding a policy does not establish that it responds to a contractually-assumed liability — a common PI exclusion. Defaults to `unverified` when absent; only a human answer moves it to yes/no.

oneOf.description: Unbounded liability held by the operating entity.
Unbounded liability with personal exposure (no entity shield, or the entity does not cure it).

tranches.description: Gompers (1995) staging: the cash cap released stepwise. A tranche with unlock_milestone_id null is unlocked from creation; others unlock via a journaled `--unlock-milestone` act. Invariant: cumulative spend ≤ cumulative unlocked tranches.

nominal_build_cap_usd.description: Optional build-cost cap (chief-wiggum#257): tokens x config/model_pricing.json, summed across every scripts/build_cost.py record attributed to this bet. Report-only (NEVER_GATES_PREFIXES 'buildcost:') until validated — checked by bet.py portfolio's build_cost_findings(). Absent -> silent, never guessed.

plan_share_cap_pct.description: Optional plan-capacity cap (chief-wiggum#257): share of the billing period's plan capacity this bet may consume, summed across every scripts/build_cost.py record attributed to this bet. Plan-share is inherently estimate-shaped (the harness rarely exposes true consumption) — report-only (NEVER_GATES_PREFIXES 'buildcost:') until validated. Absent -> silent, never guessed.
